transcript.content:
hey, i'm Berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hi Berry :) ok so the bit that stuck with me most is my mum was there, folding something really carefully, and she gave me this little red paper bird. everything in the dream was made of paper actually, it was kind of weird

everything made of paper... and a little red bird from your mum, that's lovely

what did it feel like when she handed it to you?
honestly i don't really remember how it felt, it just happened. but right after that it started raining, except the rain was all tiny paper birds, loads of them in different colours

that's fine, dreams are like that

raining paper birds though, in all different colours... wow

what happened when they reached the ground?
they just landed on the street and on people's shoulders. there were people everywhere, all flat like cardboard cutouts, all walking the same way

flat like cardboard cutouts, all walking the same way... that's eerie

were you walking with them?
i was walking too, through the city, down this narrow street with paper houses kind of leaning over it. i don't remember if i was going the same way as them though

paper houses leaning over a narrow street... i can almost see it

when you were walking down it, were you just you, or did it feel more like you were watching from somewhere outside?
i think it was just me, walking. i don't really remember it feeling like watching from outside. the weird bit was at the end though, the whole city started folding up around us

the whole city folding up around you... oh wow

what happened to you when it started folding?
the houses just folded down flat one after another, like a pop-up book closing. then it was just me and my mum standing on this big sheet of white paper. and then i woke up

just you and your mum on a big sheet of white paper... that's such a quiet way for it to end

did you still have the little red paper bird she gave you?

i don't remember actually, the dream doesn't really say what happened to it. oh and one thing i forgot, everything looked really flat, like cut out of coloured paper. bright reds and yellows and blues, no shading at all

that's fine, the bird can just stay a mystery

bright reds and yellows and blues with no shading at all, like it was all cut out of coloured paper... i love that

was there anything else in there that seemed to matter, or was it really just the little red bird?
i think that's pretty much all of it. the bird and my mum were the main things for me, and the city folding up at the end. i don't remember anything else really.

the bird, your mum, and the city folding up... that feels like the heart of it

was your mum already there folding when it began?
i don't think so, i was walking through the city first. then she was just there at a corner, already folding it when i got to her. i don't know how long she'd been there

so she was just there at a corner, already folding when you got to her

and before that, when you were walking through the city first, what's the very first bit you can remember?

i think just walking down that narrow street with the paper houses leaning over, and all the flat people going the same way. i don't remember how i got there or anything before that, it kind of starts with me already walking

ok, let me tell it back to you

it starts with you already walking through a city where everything's made of paper, flat like it's cut out of coloured paper, bright reds and yellows and blues with no shading at all. you're going down a narrow street with paper houses leaning over it, and there are people everywhere, flat like cardboard cutouts, all walking the same way. at a corner your mum is just there, already folding something really carefully, and she gives you a little red paper bird. right after that it starts raining tiny paper birds in loads of different colours, landing on the street and on people's shoulders. then the whole city starts folding up, the houses folding down flat one after another like a pop-up book closing, until it's just you and your mum standing on a big sheet of white paper. and then you wake up

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's it, you got it all right. that's pretty much exactly how it was

i'm really glad, it's such a gentle dream

would you like to see it drawn?
oh yes, i'd really like that

ok, here are a few ways it could be drawn

a) layered paper cut-outs, like a quiet handmade picture book you're standing inside. b) bold and bright, like an old poster that somehow feels calm. c) soft and flat, like a bedtime story someone drew carefully. d) just how it looked: everything cut from bright coloured paper, no shading

which one feels closest, or would you rather tell me your own way?
d i think, just bright coloured paper with no shading, that's how it looked

ok, i'll start with your mum

i'm picturing her cut from bright coloured paper like everything else, flat, no shading, her head tipped down a little and her hands busy folding, really careful and calm

is anything about her different from how you remember, or would you leave her to me?

that sounds right, she was really careful with it. i don't remember what she looked like exactly or what she was wearing, so go with your guess. she was standing at a corner of the street if that helps

ok, i'll guess her, standing at the corner, folding carefully

i'm sketching your mum now, and the paper city, the big sheet of white paper and the little red paper bird. it'll all show up on the right over the next minute or two

if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
oh wow, they're all up. yeah that looks right, the bright colours and everything flat. seeing my mum there with the little red bird is really nice

i'm really glad she feels right, her and that little red bird

and the flat people and the paper city, do they look the way you remember too?
yeah they do, the houses leaning over the street and the flat people all going the same way, that's how i remember it. it's a bit strange seeing it actually drawn

yeah, it's a funny feeling, seeing something that was only in your head sitting there on paper

i'm glad the city came out the way you remember it, leaning houses and all
yeah it really is funny. thanks for doing this Berry, it's nice having it somewhere other than just my head

i'm really glad, it was lovely hearing it

your mum and that little red bird, safe somewhere now
yeah, safe somewhere now :) thanks again Berry, i really like them

i'm so glad you like them

thanks for sharing it with me, it was a really gentle one to hear
thanks for listening to it :) bye Berry
bye :) keep that little red bird from your mum close, now it's somewhere you can look at it whenever you like

Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Move: start. They chose coloured paper cut-outs, just as it looked. Say you'll start with your mum, then describe how you picture your mum on their own, briefly, in plain words: not the scene around them, not anyone or anything else, and not the rest of the dream. From what they told you: who they are: the dreamer's mum. Then ask if anything's different, or if they'd leave it to you.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
